note: Files: A = runs/theory-rows/s3new/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl and B = runs/theory-rows/s3new/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (the script fetches each from the S3 key the recipe names, with --profile iterate-ecr, if it is missing), plus studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Both row files have 500 rows, all with sample = 0, and boolean cap_hit fields. The main ambiguity is the subject filter. per_problem.json labels subjects in lowercase snake case ('algebra', ..., 'number_theory'), so no row has subject == 'Number Theory'. Read literally, as the main number, the filter removes nothing and Number Theory problems stay in S. alt_measured excludes subject == 'number_theory', which is almost certainly what the author meant: mod arithmetic such as 17*3 = 1 would otherwise count as wrong equations. If the original computation used the intended reading, its number matches alt_measured, not measured. S also requires a kept row in both files, cap_hit false in both, and the problem_index to be present in per_problem.json (missing rows exclude the problem). The EQ regexes are copied verbatim from the recipe. Step 5's line runs from just after the previous newline to just before the next one (to the end of the text if there is none). Step 3's pre_s[-1] test uses the real newline character. '*', the times sign, \times and \cdot all map to op 'mul', so they share a tuple when deduplicating per row (step 8). The statistic sums N and W over the S rows of each file. The bootstrap resamples problems in S (each entry holds one problem's paired (N_A, W_A, N_B, W_B) counts) and recomputes R. A resample with N_A or N_B = 0 gives inf; this is only possible if the counts are tiny. If N_A or N_B is 0 on the full S, the script prints refuted_without_number, as the recipe says. n = |S| (paired, so both groups have size |S|). refuted_by is null, so refuted_by_met is always false. example_row is the A row of the first problem in S, with text cut to 300 characters and its (N_row, W_row) attached.
